screening_decisions.reason: This is a mathematical modeling study that estimates required sensitivity of POC tests. It does not report primary diagnostic accuracy data with 2x2 contingency tables comparing a POC test against NAAT in a clinical population.

This study assesses concordance between Medicare claims and SEER reports for bone metastases in prostate cancer patients. The population (prostate cancer), outcome (bone metastases), and test type (claims-based measures) do not match the review criteria for urogenital Chlamydia trachomatis POC testing.

This prospective trial evaluated rapid in-clinic tests (DFA, OIA) against PCR in 1,384 female patients at an STD clinic. It provides diagnostic performance data relevant to POC testing for Chlamydia in women of reproductive age.

This pilot study evaluated the QuickVue rapid diagnostic test against PCR for endocervical samples, reporting sensitivity and specificity data. While it is a pilot study, it provides diagnostic accuracy data for a rapid POC test against NAAT.
This is a clinical practice guideline document, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. It does not report 2x2 data comparing POC tests against NAAT.
This is a review/editorial article discussing the state of STI diagnostics and ASSURED criteria. It does not report primary diagnostic accuracy data for Chlamydia POC tests.

This prospective study evaluated two chlamydia POC tests (CRT and ACON) against NAAT in 451 men and women in Vanuatu. It reports sensitivity and specificity data with 2x2 data for both tests in men and women.

This study evaluated the Clearview Chlamydia MF rapid test against Roche Amplicor CT assay (NAAT) in 1,497 women at STD clinics in China. It reports sensitivity, specificity, and PPV for vaginal and cervical specimens.

This prospective cohort study evaluated a rapid Chlamydia test against PCR in 1,211 men aged 16-73. It reports sensitivity (82.6%), specificity (98.5%), PPV, and NPV - providing diagnostic accuracy data for a POC test in men.
This is a CDC guideline document providing recommendations for laboratory-based detection. It is not a primary diagnostic accuracy study and does not report 2x2 data for POC tests.
This is a systematic review of POC tests, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. While it summarizes diagnostic accuracy studies, it does not provide primary 2x2 data itself.
This is a summary of evidence for CDC treatment guidelines, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. It does not report 2x2 data comparing POC tests against NAAT.
This is a decision analysis/modeling study using a hypothetical cohort of 10,000 women. It does not report primary diagnostic accuracy data from actual patient testing.

This study evaluated the HandiLab-C home test against two NAATs (Roche Amplicor and Abbott m2000) in 231 women. It reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV - providing diagnostic accuracy data for a rapid POC test.
This study is about Haemophilus ducreyi (chancroid) treatment, not Chlamydia trachomatis diagnosis. The pathogen does not match the review criteria.
This paper describes the QUADAS-2 quality assessment tool for diagnostic accuracy studies. It is not itself a diagnostic accuracy study and does not report 2x2 data for Chlamydia POC tests.
This is a methodological paper about statistical analysis of diagnostic accuracy data. It does not report primary diagnostic accuracy data for Chlamydia POC tests.
This is a systematic review summarizing multiple POC test studies. It does not provide primary diagnostic accuracy data from a single study.
This is a mathematical modeling study about partner notification strategies, not a diagnostic accuracy study of POC tests. It does not report 2x2 data.

This study evaluated Clearview Chlamydia MF and CRT rapid tests against PCR in women from low- and high-risk populations in the Philippines. It reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV for both tests.
This is a methodological paper about detecting publication bias in meta-analyses of diagnostic accuracy studies. It does not report primary diagnostic accuracy data for Chlamydia POC tests.
This is a review of randomized controlled trials evaluating chlamydia screening to prevent PID. It does not report diagnostic accuracy data for POC tests against NAAT.
This is a cohort study examining risk factors for PID among sex workers. It does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy of POC tests against NAAT.
This paper discusses applying GRADE methodology to diagnostic tests. It is not a primary diagnostic accuracy study and does not report 2x2 data for Chlamydia POC tests.
This is a review article describing laboratory diagnostic methods for Chlamydia. It does not report primary diagnostic accuracy data for POC tests against NAAT.

This is a systematic review, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. The review objective is to assess clinical and cost-effectiveness, not to report diagnostic accuracy with 2x2 data. Excluded per selection criteria.
This is a systematic review of nucleic acid amplification tests, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study of rapid POC tests. Excluded per selection criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating Biostar Chlamydia OIA (rapid POC test) in women at STD clinic. Uses multiple reference standards including PCR. Reports sensitivity/specificity data. Meets inclusion criteria for diagnostic accuracy study in reproductive-age women.

This is a prevalence survey, not a diagnostic accuracy study. It assesses STI prevalence in populations, not the accuracy of POC tests against NAAT reference standard. Excluded per selection criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating rapid POC tests (ACON NG/CT duo, QuickVue Chlamydia RT) for C. trachomatis in symptomatic women aged 14-49. Uses NAAT as reference standard. Reports sensitivity and specificity. Meets inclusion criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study comparing multiple test methods including Clearview EIA (rapid in-office test) for C. trachomatis detection in women. Reports sensitivity data for different assays. Meets inclusion criteria for diagnostic accuracy study.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating BioStar Chlamydia OIA (rapid POC test) in adolescent females. Uses two NAATs as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (59.4%) and specificity (98.4%). Meets inclusion criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating Chlamydia Rapid Test (CRT) Device in asymptomatic men. Uses BD ProbeTec ET PCR as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (20%) and specificity (100%). Meets inclusion criteria for diagnostic accuracy in men of reproductive age.

This is a prevalence study, not a diagnostic accuracy study. Objective is to determine prevalence using PCR, not to evaluate accuracy of POC tests against NAAT reference. Excluded per selection criteria.

This is a review article discussing laboratory diagnostic approaches, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not report 2x2 data or evaluate specific POC tests. Excluded per selection criteria.
This is a surveillance study measuring STI prevalence and risk behaviors in FSWs and MSM. Not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating POC tests. Excluded per selection criteria.
This is a prevalence study determining prevalence and risk factors of multiple STIs. Not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating POC test performance against NAAT. Excluded per selection criteria.
Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating rapid POC test for C. trachomatis in sex workers. Uses PCR as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (62.96%) and specificity (99.60%). Meets inclusion criteria.
This is a review article discussing various diagnostic tests available. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not report 2x2 data. Excluded per selection criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating Chlamydia Rapid Test (POC) with vaginal swabs in women aged 16-54. Uses PCR and SDA as reference standards. Reports sensitivity (83.5%), specificity (98.9%), PPV, NPV. Meets inclusion criteria.

This study investigates serovar associations with symptoms, not diagnostic accuracy of POC tests. Does not evaluate index test vs reference standard for C. trachomatis detection. Excluded per selection criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating Chlamydia Rapid Test (CRT) in women at high- and low-risk STI clinics. Uses NAAT (Aptima) as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (41.2%) and specificity (96.4%). Meets inclusion criteria.
This is a review article on immune-biology of C. trachomatis infection and infertility. Not a diagnostic accuracy study. Excluded per selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about search strategies for DTA studies, not a diagnostic accuracy study itself. Excluded per selection criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating chlamydial OIA (rapid assay) in outpatients. Uses LCR as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (31.6%) and specificity (98.9%). Meets inclusion criteria for diagnostic accuracy study.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating three POC tests (Handilab-C, Biorapid CHLAMYDIA Ag, QuickVue Chlamydia) in women at STI clinic. Uses NAAT as gold standard. Reports sensitivities (12-27%). Meets inclusion criteria.
This is a review article discussing risk factors for genital chlamydia. Not a diagnostic accuracy study. Excluded per selection criteria.
This is a guidelines document for laboratory diagnosis, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Excluded per selection criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating a new prototype POC device for C. trachomatis in adolescent women. Uses cervical NAAT as gold standard. Reports sensitivity improvement from 38% to 80%. Meets inclusion criteria.
This is a retrospective chart review of treatment outcomes after positive screening. Not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating POC test performance. Excluded per selection criteria.
